Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All T are P.

All C are P.

Some O are C.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some T are C.

II. Some P are T.

III. Some P are O.

options.text: Both conclusions II and III follow
Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

All T are P.

All C are P.

Some O are C.

**Possible Venn diagram:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30e26c4fdecefd798f5f765869667b254c98862eafdb488218b86d4ab0332b7c.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some T are C → False (It is not correct because there is no definite relation between them)

II. Some P are T →** True** (Since all T are P)

III. Some P are O →** True** (Since all C are P and some O are C)

**Both conclusions II and III follow.**

Hence,** 'option 2'** is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘FIGHT’ is written as ‘45’ and ‘VENT’ is written as ‘57’.How will ‘TREND’ be written in that language?
questions.solution:
The positional values of the English alphabet is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d9f2222d13f0d75477f5789fe34c986626f9d54f937ee85ec5f0db5452d8cd8.png] 

The pattern followed here is:** Sum of positional values of all the letters - Number of letters in the word**

‘FIGHT’ is written as ‘45’ 

⇒ F(6) + I(9) + G(7) + H(8) + T(20) = 50 - 5 = **45**

And,

‘VENT’ is written as ‘57’

⇒ V(22) + E(5) + N(14) T(20) = 61 - 4 **= 57**

Similarly,

‘TREND’ will be written as:

⇒ T(20) + R(18) + E(5) + N(14) + D(4) = 61 - 5 = **56**

Hence,** 'option 3' **is the correct answer.
